Counsel,

Thank you for sending the Seller’s initial draft. Buyer has reviewed the draft and has the following comments.

Most importantly, Buyer cannot support the proposed USD 45,000,000 purchase price on the current draft and available diligence. Buyer’s counterproposal is USD 38,000,000, subject to confirmatory diligence and customary adjustments for cash, debt, working capital, transaction expenses, and any leakage.

We also propose that closing occur no earlier than 45 days after signing and remain subject to customary closing conditions, including completion of confirmatory diligence, receipt of required approvals, and no material adverse change.

The representations section should be expanded beyond the financial statements to include customary representations regarding authority, title to the shares, capitalization, no conflicts, compliance with law, taxes, material contracts, litigation, employees and benefits, intellectual property, privacy/data, environmental matters, undisclosed liabilities, and absence of material adverse change.

Please also add customary indemnification provisions, including survival periods, escrow or holdback, baskets, caps, and appropriate exclusions for fraud, taxes, fundamental representations, title/capitalization matters, and known issues identified in diligence.

Finally, the confidentiality covenant should include standard exceptions for disclosures to representatives, financing sources, regulators, and disclosures required by law.

Please circulate a revised draft reflecting these points, or let us know if you would prefer to discuss.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,500,000 for the Shares, subject to customary adjustments for cash, indebtedness, net working capital against a mutually agreed target, and unpaid transaction expenses, in each case calculated in accordance with this Agreement and consistent with the Company’s historical accounting practices.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur as promptly as practicable following satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement, and in any event no later than 35 days after signing, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the parties. The obligation of each party to close shall be subject only to customary conditions, including receipt of required governmental and material third-party approvals, accuracy of the other party’s fundamental representations in all material respects, compliance in all material respects with pre-closing covenants, and the absence of any law or order prohibiting the transactions. Buyer’s confirmatory diligence shall be completed prior to signing and shall not be a condition to Closing. Buyer’s obligation to close shall also be subject to the absence of a Material Adverse Effect with respect to the Company after signing.

3. Representations. The Seller shall make customary representations and warranties, subject to agreed disclosure schedules and appropriate materiality and knowledge qualifiers, regarding: (a) Seller’s organization, power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) Seller’s title to the Shares, free and clear of liens other than restrictions arising under applicable securities laws or this Agreement; (c) capitalization of the Company; (d) no conflicts with Seller’s organizational documents, applicable law or material contracts; (e) accuracy of the Company’s financial statements in all material respects; (f) compliance with applicable laws in all material respects; (g) taxes; (h) material contracts; (i) litigation; (j) employees and benefit plans; (k) intellectual property; (l) privacy and data security; (m) environmental matters; (n) absence of undisclosed liabilities required to be reflected under applicable accounting principles; and (o) absence of a Material Adverse Effect since the date of the most recent financial statements. Buyer shall make customary representations regarding organization, authority, enforceability, no conflicts, availability of funds, investment intent and broker fees.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement and all non-public information exchanged in connection with the transactions are confidential and shall not be disclosed by either party except to its affiliates and representatives who need to know such information and are informed of its confidential nature, to debt or equity financing sources and their representatives in connection with the transactions, to governmental authorities or regulators in connection with required approvals, or as required by applicable law, legal process or stock exchange rules; provided that, to the extent legally permissible, the disclosing party shall give the other party prompt notice and reasonably cooperate to limit the scope of such disclosure.

5. Indemnification. From and after Closing, each party shall indemnify the other party and its affiliates and representatives for losses arising from breaches of such party’s representations, warranties and covenants and, with respect to Seller, pre-Closing taxes of the Company. Non-fundamental representations shall survive for 12 months after Closing, fundamental representations shall survive for 6 years after Closing, tax representations and pre-Closing tax indemnities shall survive until 60 days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations, and covenants shall survive in accordance with their terms. Claims for breaches of non-fundamental representations shall be subject to a deductible basket equal to 1.0% of the Purchase Price and an aggregate cap equal to 10.0% of the Purchase Price. Claims for breaches of fundamental representations, title to the Shares, capitalization, fraud, willful misconduct, equitable remedies, and pre-Closing taxes shall not be subject to the basket or general cap and shall be capped at the Purchase Price except in the case of fraud. At Closing, 5.0% of the Purchase Price shall be deposited into escrow for 12 months as Buyer’s sole source of recovery for breaches of non-fundamental representations, absent fraud or willful misconduct. The parties shall negotiate in good faith appropriate special indemnities for specific known matters identified in diligence, if any, with scope, duration and cap to be agreed.

A counter at USD 39.5M leaves room while anchoring below likely settlement. Also request buyer-protective adjustments: defined NWC target before signing, 45-day outside or at least practical approval timing, full bring-down of business reps subject to MAE/materiality scrape, better escrow/cap/basket, and special indemnities for diligence items.

receiver.requested_changes: Buyer can proceed without a broad post-signing diligence condition only if the economics and closing protection reflect that risk allocation. Buyer requests: (1) Purchase Price reduced to USD 39,500,000, subject to customary cash-free/debt-free, NWC and transaction expense adjustments; (2) NWC target to be agreed and expressly stated before signing, with an attached illustrative calculation based on historical practices; (3) Closing outside date extended to 45 days after signing, or alternatively 35 days only if all required third-party and governmental approvals are specifically identified and Seller bears the risk of delay except where caused by Buyer breach; (4) Buyer closing condition to include accuracy of Seller and Company representations, with fundamental reps true in all respects except de minimis inaccuracies and other reps true except where failure would not reasonably be expected to be material to the Company, plus no MAE; (5) Seller reps to be made by Seller regarding the Company, not merely listed as topics, and to include ordinary course since latest financials, customers/suppliers, anti-corruption/sanctions, insurance, real property/assets sufficiency, and no undisclosed liabilities; (6) indemnity basket reduced to 0.5% of Purchase Price as a true deductible or, preferably, a tipping basket at 0.75%; (7) general cap increased to 15% of Purchase Price; (8) escrow increased to 7.5% of Purchase Price for 15 months, and not the sole source for breaches involving knowing breach, equitable remedies, purchase price adjustment, special indemnities, taxes, fundamental reps or fraud; (9) express materiality scrape for determining breach and losses; (10) special indemnities to be identified and agreed before signing for any diligence matters; and (11) reinstate a confidentiality provision and add ordinary interim operating covenants.
receiver.message_back:
Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. Buyer appreciates Seller’s movement and is prepared to continue working toward a signable agreement without a broad post-signing confirmatory diligence condition, provided the economics and risk allocation are adjusted accordingly.

On price, Buyer’s counter is USD 39,500,000, subject to customary cash, debt, net working capital and unpaid transaction expense adjustments. Buyer is taking on incremental risk by completing confirmatory work pre-signing and accepting a limited interim period, and that needs to be reflected in the headline price and indemnity package.

Buyer also requests the following revisions:

1. Net working capital. The NWC target and methodology should be agreed before signing and attached to the agreement, including an illustrative calculation based on the Company’s historical accounting practices.

2. Closing timing. Buyer continues to prefer a 45-day outside date. If Seller requires 35 days, then the required governmental and material third-party approvals should be specifically identified before signing, and delay risk should not fall on Buyer absent Buyer breach.

3. Closing conditions. Buyer’s closing condition should include accuracy of Seller/Company fundamental reps in all respects except de minimis inaccuracies, and other reps except where inaccuracies would not reasonably be expected to be material to the Company, together with no MAE and covenant compliance.

4. Representations. The draft should state the actual Seller representations regarding the Company rather than a topic list. Please add ordinary course since the latest financials, customers/suppliers, anti-corruption and sanctions, insurance, real property/assets sufficiency, and no undisclosed liabilities.

5. Indemnity. Buyer requests a 0.5% deductible basket or, alternatively, a 0.75% tipping basket; a 15% general cap; and a 7.5% escrow for 15 months. The escrow should not be the sole source for purchase price adjustment, taxes, fundamental reps, special indemnities, knowing breach, equitable remedies, or fraud. Please also add a materiality scrape for breach and loss calculations.

6. Special indemnities. Any specific diligence matters should be addressed before signing with appropriate special indemnities.

7. Other provisions. Please reinstate confidentiality and add customary interim operating covenants.

If Seller can move on price and the above protections, Buyer believes the parties should be able to resolve the remaining points promptly this week.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
